The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.

12.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
12.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
12.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

13.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
13.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

14.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
14.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
14.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

15.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
15.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

16.meaning: He disbelieves / rejects / covers up — the present-tense act of denying or being ungrateful, refusing to accept the truth; done by a single male (or impersonal) subject.
16.grammar: Present/imperfect tense. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final '-u' ending is the indicative mood, the default form for a simple ongoing or habitual statement ('he disbelieves').
16.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and thus reject or be ungrateful

17.meaning: A phrase meaning 'some of you' or 'one part of you'. It singles out a portion of an addressed group, often paired with 'to/for another' to express a reciprocal relationship within that group.
17.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part/some' carrying the -u ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or doer in its clause. The attached -kum means 'of you all' (plural), so the whole means 'some part of you'.

18.meaning: 'In part / in some' — referring to a portion or some of a whole, here left indefinite. The bi- prefix gives the sense of disbelieving 'in' something.
18.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with') plus the noun baʿḍ ('a part, some'). The final -in (tanwīn kasr) is the genitive case with indefiniteness, required after bi- and marking the noun as 'some (unspecified) part.'
18.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

19.meaning: "And he curses" — to curse (laʿana) is to cast someone far from mercy and blessing, to declare them banished from favor.
19.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ya- prefix means 'he' (or an unspecified masculine subject). The final -u is the normal indicative ending of the present tense: it signals a plain ongoing or habitual statement — 'he curses / does curse' — not a command or wish.
19.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, banish from mercy

20.meaning: A phrase meaning 'some of you' or 'one part of you'. It singles out a portion of an addressed group, often paired with 'to/for another' to express a reciprocal relationship within that group.
20.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part/some' carrying the -u ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or doer in its clause. The attached -kum means 'of you all' (plural), so the whole means 'some part of you'.

21.meaning: Some, a part, or one of a group — 'another' when paired with 'one'. It singles out an unspecified portion or member set against the rest.

parts.en: some / a part / one (of a group)

21.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part / some'. The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case used for a direct object. Paired with baʿḍ ('another'), it builds the sense 'one another / each other'.
21.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, a portion, some of a whole

22.meaning: And your abode / and your dwelling — the final dwelling place of the disbelievers, which is the Fire.

parts.en: your abode / your dwelling / your refuge (nominative with possessive)

22.grammar: Conjunction waw + noun maʾwā (abode, dwelling, refuge, place of shelter) from the root ʾ-w-y (to take shelter, to lodge), with second-person masculine plural possessive suffix -kum (and the connector vowel -u before the next word). Nominative or as predicate.
22.root: أ-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to take shelter, lodge, give refuge; abode

23.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
23.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

24.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
24.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

25.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
25.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

26.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
26.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

27.meaning: Helpers / supporters: those who give aid, support, and victory to another, standing by them against an adversary; the plural of 'helper'.
27.grammar: A masculine plural active participle — a 'doer' word meaning 'ones who help'. The sound plural ending -īna marks more than two; this -īna form (rather than -ūna) is the case used for objects of verbs and after prepositions or in possession (the accusative/genitive).
27.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to give victory/support

1.meaning: Then he believed — he came to faith, trusted, and gave assent. The prefixed 'then/so' marks this believing as a consequence or next step following something prior.
1.grammar: 'Then/so' + a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular. The fa- prefix links the action as a result or sequel ('so then…'). The verb's -a ending is the past-tense marker for 'he,' and this form-IV pattern (ā-a-a) carries the sense of attaining faith and giving secure trust.
1.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security; hence to trust and believe

2.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

3.meaning: Lūṭ (Lot) — the prophet sent to the people of the overturned cities, nephew and companion of Ibrahim.
3.grammar: A proper name. The -un ending is the nominative case: it typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action ('Lut did/said/believed…').

4.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
4.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.
4.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

5.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
5.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

6.meaning: One who emigrates; a person actively leaving home and homeland for the sake of Allah. The muhājir abandons what is familiar in order to move toward his Lord.
6.grammar: An active participle: the mu- prefix turns the verb 'to emigrate' into 'one who emigrates'. The -un ending is nominative and indefinite: it typically marks the subject of a sentence or the predicate 'I am / he is (an emigrant)'.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
7.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

8.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
8.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

9.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
9.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

10.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
10.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

11.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
11.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

12.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
12.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
12.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

1.meaning: 'And We bestowed / granted' — to give freely as a gift or favour, with no expectation of return, prefixed with 'and'.

parts.en: bestowed, granted as a gift (past stem)

1.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we', giving 'and we bestowed'.
1.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, to bestow as a gift

2.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

3.meaning: Isaac (Isḥāq) — the proper name of the prophet, son of Abraham.
3.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is a 'diptote', meaning it takes the '-a' ending for both the accusative (direct object) and genitive cases and never takes nunation ('-an').

4.meaning: The proper name 'Jacob' (Yaʿqūb), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
4.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; as a foreign (non-Arabic) name it is 'diptote,' taking -a for both those cases and never taking nunation (the -n sound).
4.root: — (proper name)

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We made / appointed / rendered.' This very common verb can mean to create or place something, or to assign something a state or role (to make X into Y).
5.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers. The verb often takes two objects, meaning 'to make/turn one thing into another.'
5.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: 'His offspring / his descendants' — the line of children and posterity issuing from a person, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
7.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). Its final tāʾ marbūṭa, normally a soft '-a', is sounded as a full '-t-' once a suffix follows; the '-i' on it is genitive, used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… of …'), and the pronoun appears as '-hi' because of it.
7.root: ذ-ر-ر / ذ-ر-أ (dh-r-r / dh-r-ʾ) — to scatter, to multiply (offspring); progeny

8.meaning: 'Prophethood' — the abstract noun for the office, status, and mission of being a prophet (nabī), one who receives revelation from Allah and conveys it. It names the divinely granted vocation itself rather than the person.
8.grammar: The al- prefix is the definite article ('the'); note that after al- the n of nubuwwa is doubled in pronunciation (assimilation). The tā' marbūṭa forms an abstract feminine noun naming a state or office. The final -a is the accusative ending, used for a direct object or item under the sway of certain particles.
8.root: ن-ب-و / ن-ب-ي (n-b-w/y) — to be high, elevated, prominent (hence nabī, a prophet)

9.meaning: 'And the Scripture / the Book' — al-kitāb is the written record or revealed Book, here joined by 'and.' Beyond a physical book, kitāb connotes a binding, prescribed writ; the root sense is of writing things down and so decreeing them.
9.grammar: Begins with wa- ('and') and carries the definite article al- ('the'). Kitāb is a verbal noun from 'to write,' used for that which is written. The final -a is the accusative ending, the case for a direct object or a noun governed by certain particles.

10.meaning: 'And We gave/granted him' — a verb of bestowing or handing over something, with 'We' as the giver and 'him' as the recipient. The root conveys the act of bringing or delivering a thing to someone so that they come to possess it.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern (afʿala: 'to give/bring to'). The suffix -nā is the subject 'we' (the doers of the giving). The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it' (the one given to). So the form packs subject and object into one word: 'we-gave-him'.
10.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in this causative form, to bring/give

11.meaning: "His reward" — ajr is a wage or recompense: payment justly due for work done, used especially of the recompense Allah grants for faith and good deeds.
11.grammar: Noun with an attached pronoun. The -a before the pronoun is the accusative ending, typically marking the word as the object of a verb ('We gave him his reward'). The suffix -hu means 'his/him', pointing back to a male person already mentioned.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
13.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
13.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

14.meaning: A linkage of 'and' with the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') plus 'he' — meaning 'and truly he…', opening a clause with firm assurance about the person referred to.
14.grammar: 'wa' is the connector 'and'. 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached -hu ('he/him') is the subject of the inna-clause, expressed in object form as inna requires.

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
16.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
16.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

17.meaning: An emphatic 'truly/surely' joined to the preposition min ('from, among, of') — conveying 'surely (one) of / among', stressing belonging to a group.
17.grammar: Two particles. 'la-' is the emphatic prefix adding certainty (often paired with inna). 'min' is a preposition meaning 'from/among/of' and puts the noun after it into the genitive case. Its final -a here is a connecting vowel used before the definite article 'al-'.

18.meaning: The righteous, upright, and morally sound ones — people who are good, virtuous, and act rightly, putting things into proper order. Plural and referring to people.
18.grammar: A definite noun/adjective ('al-' = 'the') in the sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in its accusative/genitive (object or 'of/from') form — the form used as a direct object or after a preposition; the parallel subject form would be -ūna.
18.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — soundness, righteousness, setting things right

1.meaning: 'And Lot (Lūṭ)' — the proper name of the prophet, prefixed with 'and'.
1.grammar: A proper name prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). Unusually for a foreign name, it is treated as fully declinable here: the '-an' ending marks the accusative case (the direct object) together with nunation ('-n').

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

3.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
3.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

4.meaning: 'To/for his people' — a compound joining the preposition 'to/for', the noun 'people' (a community or folk, especially one's own kinfolk and nation), and 'his'. It expresses a community belonging to, or addressed by, a single male individual.
4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') governs the noun, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending — the case that regularly follows a preposition or links one noun to another ('… of …'). The attached -hi means 'his'; the i-vowel form -hi (rather than -hu) is used because it harmonises with the preceding -i sound.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

5.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
5.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.

6.meaning: You surely do approach / come to — emphatic assertion that 'you' (a group) indeed do or come to (some act). Combines an emphasis particle with the verb 'you (all) come to'.
6.grammar: A present/imperfect verb fronted by the emphatic prefix la- ('surely, indeed'), which stresses the truth of the statement. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood: 'you all surely do come to'.
6.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, approach; figuratively to do or perpetrate

7.meaning: 'The immorality' / 'the gross indecency' — a flagrant, shameful act; an enormity that exceeds the bounds of decency. With the article it denotes the gross indecent act.
7.grammar: A definite feminine singular noun. The -a ending is the accusative case, marking it as the object of a verb (the thing committed or done).

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: He/it preceded you / came before you — he went ahead of, or did something earlier than, 'you' (a group). Combines the verb 'he preceded' with the object 'you all'.
9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb denoting a completed action. The verb's bare form (ending -a before the suffix) marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all', the ones preceded.
9.root: س-ب-ق (s-b-q) — to precede, go before, outstrip

10.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
10.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
12.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.

13.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
13.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

14.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
14.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
14.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: A charged question-opener meaning roughly 'Is it really the case that you (plural)…?' — a questioning particle fused with an emphasis particle (inna, 'indeed/truly') and 'you'. It poses a question while underscoring the claim being questioned, often with a tone of astonishment or challenge.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix a- ('do/is it that…?') joined to the emphasizing particle inna ('indeed'). Inna places the noun or pronoun following it (its ism) in the accusative; here that is the attached -kum ('you', plural), which functions logically like the subject of the statement but stands formally in the accusative. The combination both asks and stresses, and the -kum addresses a group.

2.meaning: You surely do approach / come to — emphatic assertion that 'you' (a group) indeed do or come to (some act). Combines an emphasis particle with the verb 'you (all) come to'.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb fronted by the emphatic prefix la- ('surely, indeed'), which stresses the truth of the statement. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood: 'you all surely do come to'.
2.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, approach; figuratively to do or perpetrate

3.meaning: The men — adult males; the plural of 'rajul' (man), made definite by 'the'.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun. The prefixed al- ('the') has its 'l' assimilated into the following 'r' (pronounced ar-rijāl). The final -a marks the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
3.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man; manhood, the male of the species

4.meaning: "And you (all) cut off / sever" — qaṭaʿa is to cut through something; with a road or path it means to waylay, block, or rob travelers; with ties it means to sever them.
4.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a group. The ta- prefix marks 'you'; the -ūna ending makes it plural masculine and indicative — 'you all are doing / habitually do' the action, stated as fact rather than commanded.
4.root: ق-ط-ع (q-ṭ-ʿ) — to cut, sever

5.meaning: 'The way, the path, the road' — used both for a physical route and, very commonly, for the figurative 'path' of right conduct, religion, or a course of action.
5.grammar: A definite noun: the al- prefix means 'the'. The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or signals an adverbial sense.

6.meaning: "And you (all) come to / commit" — atā means to come to something; when followed by a deed it means to approach and commit it, to 'go in for' an act.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a group. The ta- prefix means 'you' and the -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the plain indicative: it describes what the group actually does, as an ongoing or habitual action.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: "Your gathering-place / assembly" — a nādī is the place or council where people gather and converse; the word for a communal meeting spot, from the same root as 'to call out'.
8.grammar: Noun with an attached pronoun. The suffix -kum means 'your' addressed to a group of people; the extra -u at its end is simply a helping vowel that smooths the join to a following word. The long -ī of nādī absorbs the case vowel, so no separate case ending is heard.
8.root: ن-د-و (n-d-w) — to call out; gathering, assembly

9.meaning: Rejection, disapproval, denial — literally 'that which is rejected/disowned.' The word munkar names anything the sound heart and revealed law refuse to accept; as a feeling on the face it means visible displeasure and hostile denial.
9.grammar: Munkar is a passive participle of the Form IV verb ankara ('to reject, disavow'), so it literally means 'that which is disavowed.' The final -a is the accusative case ending, the case a noun typically takes when it is the object of a verb ('you recognize the disapproval').
9.root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r) — to refuse to recognize, disavow, find strange

10.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
10.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

11.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

11.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

12.meaning: An answer, a reply, a response given back to something said or asked.
12.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -a marks the accusative case, typically used for the direct object of a verb. If it heads a possessive (iḍāfa) construction, this same accusative ending stays on it ('the answer of …'), since only the following, possessed noun takes the genitive.

13.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
13.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
13.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
15.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

16.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
16.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

17.meaning: 'Come!' (to more than one person, or with the sense 'come to us') — a command to approach or come forward. The base verb means to come or arrive.
17.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to someone, built on the verb 'to come.' Its initial vowel is a helping (connecting) vowel that lets the consonant cluster be pronounced. The attached -nā means 'us,' giving the sense 'come to us.'
17.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to arrive, to bring

18.meaning: With/of a punishment: 'with' joined to a word for a chastisement, torment, or penalty inflicted as recompense; indefinite ('a punishment').
18.grammar: An indefinite noun with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / of'). The ending -in does two things: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a punishment'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case required after the preposition 'bi-'.

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
20.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

21.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
21.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
21.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

22.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
22.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

23.meaning: The truthful ones — those who are sincere and speak the truth, whose words and deeds match reality. A plural describing people characterized by truthfulness and sincerity, prefixed with 'the.'
23.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('the ones who are truthful') with the definite article 'the.' The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive (oblique) form: it marks the word either as an object of a verb or as following a preposition or possessive, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
23.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, telling the truth

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
2.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

3.meaning: "Help me!" — a direct plea for aid. Naṣr is help that brings victory: support given so that a person prevails over what opposes him.
3.grammar: An imperative (command form) addressed to one person: unṣur means 'give help!'. The suffix -nī means 'me' (its n is a buffer letter that regularly appears before the 'me' pronoun on verbs). Together: a one-word petition, 'help me'.

4.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
4.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
4.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

5.meaning: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
5.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

6.meaning: Those who spread corruption / the workers of mischief — people who ruin, disorder, and lay waste, the opposite of those who set things right.
6.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the.' An active participle (the one who corrupts) from the causative form (afʿala). The '-īna' ending is the masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case — the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition.
6.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — to be corrupt, spoil, cause ruin/disorder

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: she/it came / arrived. A verb of coming, arriving, or presenting itself, in the feminine.
2.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The suffix -t marks a single feminine subject: 'she/it came.' Past tense presents the arrival as already accomplished.

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'messengers' joined to 'our' — those sent with a message or commission, envoys; in scripture, the prophets sent by Allah. The form means 'our messengers.'
3.grammar: rusul is the plural of rasūl ('messenger/envoy'). The vowel -u before the pronoun is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject/doer ('the messengers [did]…'). The attached -nā is the possessive 'our.'
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one sent with it

4.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
4.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.
4.root: — (proper name)

5.meaning: With glad tidings / bearing good news. It conveys coming with or carrying joyful news — an announcement of something happy and welcome.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by means of') plus the definite article al- ('the') plus the noun bushrā ('glad tidings'). Nouns ending in this long -ā do not show a separate case vowel; the genitive expected after the preposition is understood but not pronounced.

6.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

7.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
7.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

8.meaning: "Destroyers of / about to destroy" — a plural participle from ahlaka, 'to destroy, bring to ruin'; it describes those who are (or are about to be) the agents of a destruction.

parts.en: plural ending (linked to a following word)

8.grammar: An active participle of the causative verb form ('to make perish'). The mu- prefix means 'ones who do' the action. The -ū ending is the masculine plural; its final n (-ūna) has been dropped because the word is bound to a following word — a construct meaning 'destroyers OF …'. Participles like this often carry a near-future sense: 'about to destroy'.

9.meaning: People of / folk of / those belonging to — the family, followers, or possessors of something (as in 'people of the Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with a thing.
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('people OF …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
9.root: ء-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to

10.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
10.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

11.meaning: A settled place where people live — a town, village, or populated locality. It denotes a community gathered in one inhabited place.
11.grammar: A feminine singular noun marked with 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding preposition or oath particle, or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …').
11.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — gathering, bringing together (people in a settlement)

12.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
12.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

13.meaning: Its people, its inhabitants, its folk — those who belong to a place or household. The base word 'ahl' denotes the people proper to something: the members of a family, the residents of a town, or those entitled to a thing.
13.grammar: A noun carrying the accusative -a ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb or the subject following certain particles. The attached suffix -hā means 'its/her', here referring back to a feminine or non-human entity (such as a town); it shows possession ('its people').
13.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — belonging, family, being a member of a household or community

14.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
14.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: Those who do wrong — wrongdoers who put things out of their right place: unjust people, oppressors, and especially those who transgress against the truth and against the rights of Allah or of others. The root sense is placing something where it does not belong.
15.grammar: This is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — the form used when the word is an object, or follows a preposition, or is linked to a preceding noun ('of the wrongdoers').

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
2.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

3.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
3.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

4.meaning: Lut (Lot), the prophet, named as the object/recipient of an action.
4.grammar: A proper name in the object case: the final -an (nunation) marks it as the direct object of a verb (the one to whom or about whom the action is done). As a name it has no root.
4.root: — (proper name)

5.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

6.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
6.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

7.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
7.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

8.meaning: 'With / about whom,' or 'than who.' It combines the preposition bi- ('with, by, about') with the relative/interrogative 'who,' referring to a person or persons — 'the one(s) who.'
8.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/about') joined to man ('who'). The word man does not change its ending for case; it can act as a question word ('who?') or as a relative word ('the one who'), and bi- supplies the sense 'with/about whom.'

9.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
9.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

10.meaning: "We will most surely save him" — a doubly emphasized divine promise of rescue, from najjā, 'to save, deliver to safety'.
10.grammar: A present/future verb loaded with emphasis. The la- prefix means 'surely'; nu- means 'we'; the stem is the intensive form 'to rescue'. The -anna ending is the 'heavy nūn' of emphasis — it stamps the statement as an unbreakable oath-like promise ('most certainly will'). The final -hu means 'him'.

11.meaning: And his household — his family and the people belonging to his home and close kin.
11.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a singular noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending marks the accusative case, used for the direct object of a verb or what is joined to one. So it reads 'and his family'.
11.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — to be settled, belong; family, kin, people of a place

12.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
12.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

13.meaning: A woman, specifically a wife — a man's spouse.
13.grammar: A singular feminine noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'), giving 'his wife'. The -a ending marks the accusative case, used for the direct object of a verb or what is grammatically joined to it.
13.root: م-ر-ء (m-r-ʾ) — relating to a person; the feminine denotes 'woman'

14.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she was / it was / it became' — from the core verb of being, linking a subject to a description or state, often setting it in past or established time.
14.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb of being. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it was'. As a being-verb it normally introduces a description of that subject.
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
15.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

16.meaning: Those who remain behind and stay put — people who linger, are left behind, and so perish with a place rather than leaving it; literally 'those who tarry / pass away'.
16.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) with the definite article al- ('the'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case — used for an object or after a preposition. So it reads 'the ones who stayed behind'.
16.root: غ-ب-ر (gh-b-r) — to remain, stay behind, linger; also dust

1.meaning: "And when…" — lammā is a time-word introducing a past event: 'at the moment that / once (something happened)'. It sets up a clause of the type 'when X happened, then Y'.
1.grammar: A particle, so it takes no case endings. Wa- simply joins it to what came before ('and'). Lammā points backward in time: it introduces a completed event and signals that a consequence follows — the reader expects 'when …, then …'.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
2.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

3.meaning: she/it came / arrived. A verb of coming, arriving, or presenting itself, in the feminine.
3.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The suffix -t marks a single feminine subject: 'she/it came.' Past tense presents the arrival as already accomplished.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'messengers' joined to 'our' — those sent with a message or commission, envoys; in scripture, the prophets sent by Allah. The form means 'our messengers.'
4.grammar: rusul is the plural of rasūl ('messenger/envoy'). The vowel -u before the pronoun is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject/doer ('the messengers [did]…'). The attached -nā is the possessive 'our.'
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one sent with it

5.meaning: Lut (Lot), the prophet, named as the object/recipient of an action.
5.grammar: A proper name in the object case: the final -an (nunation) marks it as the direct object of a verb (the one to whom or about whom the action is done). As a name it has no root.

6.meaning: He/it was made to feel bad, grieved, or troubled; the experience of being distressed by something.
6.grammar: A passive past-tense verb ('he was distressed/made to feel ill at ease'); the inner vowel shift to -ī- marks the passive of a hollow verb (one with a weak middle root letter). Third-person masculine singular ('he/it') is shown by the absence of any added subject suffix (a zero ending); the final fatḥa is simply the vowel on the last root letter.

7.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
7.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

8.meaning: And it became narrow/tight; the act of being constrained or straitened, joined by 'and'.
8.grammar: Past-tense hollow verb (one with a weak middle root letter). Third-person masculine singular ('he/it') is shown by the absence of any added subject suffix (a zero ending); the final fatḥa is just the vowel on the last root letter. The prefixed wa- is the connective 'and'. Often paired with 'dharʿan' to mean 'felt unable to cope'.

9.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
9.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

10.meaning: In capacity or ability to cope — literally the reach of one's arm; used to specify the respect in which one feels constrained ('straitened in coping').
10.grammar: A noun in the accusative used as a specifier ('as to one's coping-capacity'), clarifying in what respect something applies. The final -an (nunation) marks this indefinite accusative of specification.
10.root: ذ-ر-ع (dh-r-ʿ) — the forearm; by extension, capacity or ability to cope

11.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
11.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: Do not fear; do not be afraid. A command form telling someone to refrain from fear.
13.grammar: A second-person masculine singular verb ('you') in the jussive mood, shown by the cut-off final consonant with no extra vowel. This clipped form is what follows a negative command particle, giving the sense 'do not fear'.
13.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, dread, being afraid

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'do not grieve / feel no sorrow' — to be saddened, anxious, or sorrowful. In a prohibition it tells someone (singular male) not to be distressed.
15.grammar: An imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, in the jussive mood (shown by the silent/sukūn ending on the final consonant rather than a vowel). This jussive form is the one used after the prohibitive particle 'lā' to express 'do not...,' i.e., a command not to grieve. The ta- prefix marks 'you (one man)' as the addressee.

16.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
16.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

17.meaning: "Your rescuers / (ones) saving you" — a plural participle from najjā, 'to save': those who are delivering someone to safety.
17.grammar: An active participle of the intensive verb form 'to rescue'. Mu- means 'ones who do' it; the -ū is the masculine plural ending whose final n has dropped because the word is bound directly to its object — 'rescuers OF you'. The suffix -ka means 'you' (addressed to one male). Such participles often promise the near future: 'we are going to save you'.

18.meaning: 'And your family / household' — ahl are the people who belong to one: one's family, kin, or the folk closely associated with a place or thing.
18.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The noun ahl carries the accusative -a ending (typically marking a direct object), and the attached -ka is the possessor 'your' (addressed to a single male).
18.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinfolk, the people belonging to a household or place; being fit/worthy.

19.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
19.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

20.meaning: A noun meaning 'your wife / the woman of (a man),' from a word denoting an adult woman. With the possessive it specifies a man's wife.
20.grammar: Feminine noun in a possessive construction with the attached pronoun '-ka' ('your,' to one male). The 'a' that appears before the pronoun is the inherent linking vowel of the feminine ending (tā marbūṭa) that surfaces whenever a suffix is attached; it is present in every case (nominative, accusative, genitive) and so does not by itself mark which case the word is in.
20.root: م-ر-أ (m-r-ʾ) — relating to a person; (feminine) woman

21.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she was / it was / it became' — from the core verb of being, linking a subject to a description or state, often setting it in past or established time.
21.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb of being. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it was'. As a being-verb it normally introduces a description of that subject.
21.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

22.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
22.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

23.meaning: Those who remain behind and stay put — people who linger, are left behind, and so perish with a place rather than leaving it; literally 'those who tarry / pass away'.
23.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) with the definite article al- ('the'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case — used for an object or after a preposition. So it reads 'the ones who stayed behind'.
23.root: غ-ب-ر (gh-b-r) — to remain, stay behind, linger; also dust

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: "Ones sending down / who will bring down" — a plural participle from anzala, 'to send down from above', used of what descends by Allah's command (revelation, rain, or punishment).
2.grammar: An active participle of the causative verb 'to make descend'. Mu- means 'ones who do' the action. The full -ūna ending is the masculine plural in the nominative case: it typically marks the word as subject or as the predicate 'we/they are ones sending down'. Participles like this often carry a near-future sense: 'about to send down'.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
3.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

4.meaning: People of / folk of / those belonging to — the family, followers, or possessors of something (as in 'people of the Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with a thing.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('people OF …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
4.root: ء-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to

5.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
5.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

6.meaning: A settled place where people live — a town, village, or populated locality. It denotes a community gathered in one inhabited place.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun marked with 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding preposition or oath particle, or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …').
6.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — gathering, bringing together (people in a settlement)

7.meaning: 'A torment / plague / punishment / scourge'. It names a defiling, distressing affliction sent as a penalty — a foul, agitating chastisement.
7.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the accusative used indefinitely — typically the direct object of a verb ('He sent down a punishment'). The nunation signals 'a/an', i.e. some unspecified instance.

8.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
8.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

9.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
9.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

10.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
10.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

11.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
11.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

12.meaning: 'They rebel / act wickedly / defiantly disobey'. The core sense is breaking away from obedience — stepping outside the bounds of what is lawful and right, like a fruit bursting out of its skin.
12.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the third-person masculine plural ('they …'). The full -ūna ending is the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of habitual or ongoing action ('they keep disobeying').
12.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to depart from obedience, rebel, act wickedly

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: "We left / We have left behind" — taraka is to leave something in place, to leave behind as a lasting trace or legacy.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -nā means 'we' as the doers: 'we left'. In the Qur'an this 'We' is Allah speaking of Himself in the majestic plural. Past-tense verbs like this take no case endings; the subject is carried entirely by the suffix.

3.meaning: "From it / of it" — the preposition 'from' joined to the pronoun 'it/her', expressing source or origin: out of it, concerning it, some of it.
3.grammar: A preposition fused with a pronoun, so there is no case ending to parse. Min expresses 'from / out of / some of'; the suffix -hā means 'it' or 'her', referring back to something grammatically feminine (a city, an event, a thing) already mentioned.

4.meaning: 'A sign / token / mark' — āyah is a sign that points to something beyond itself; it also denotes a miraculous proof and a verse of revelation.
4.grammar: A singular noun. The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing pointed to or presented), or stands as the predicate of certain particles.
4.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token

5.meaning: A clear sign; manifest evidence. A bayyina is proof so plain that it distinguishes truth from falsehood by itself — something made luminously evident.
5.grammar: A noun from the root 'to be clear/distinct', on an intensive pattern: not just clear but self-evidently clear. The -an ending (heard as -tan because of the feminine -t-) is the accusative indefinite: it typically marks the object of a verb or a descriptive phrase 'as a clear sign'.

6.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
6.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

7.meaning: They use their reason, they understand and reflect; to grasp things with the intellect and restrain oneself accordingly.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -na ending also signals the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action ('they use reason').
7.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand; to restrain (as a tether restrains)

1.meaning: "and to / toward" — the connective "and" joined to the preposition meaning "to, toward, up to (an end-point)."
1.grammar: A particle cluster: the connective wa- ("and") plus the preposition ilā ("to/toward"), which indicates direction or destination and puts the following noun into the genitive case. Particles do not inflect.

2.meaning: Madyan (Midian) — the proper name of an ancient people and the land they inhabited.
2.grammar: A proper name. As a diptote (not fully declinable) noun, it takes a single -a ending in place of both accusative and genitive and does not receive tanwīn. It names a people and their territory.

3.meaning: "their brother" — the noun "brother" (a male sibling, or by extension a kinsman/fellow member of a community) with the possessor "their."
3.grammar: "Brother" is one of the special "five nouns" whose case is shown by a long vowel: the -ā here marks the accusative (object) state. The suffix -hum means "their," referring to a group of males.

4.meaning: Shuʿayb — the proper name of a prophet sent to the people of Madyan.
4.grammar: A proper name (the diminutive form of a name) that is fully declinable (triptote). The -an ending marks the accusative case — fitting when the name is the one being sent or mentioned as object. The tanwīn here signals that the name belongs to the fully declinable class, not indefiniteness, since a proper name is inherently definite.

5.meaning: 'Then he said / so he said' — the past-tense verb 'he said,' introduced by a connector meaning 'then / so,' marking what follows as the next or resulting step.
5.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then / so,' linking this to what came before and often implying sequence or consequence. The verb is past-tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final -a is the base vowel of the 3rd-person masculine singular past form, marking that a single masculine subject performed the action.

6.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
6.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

7.meaning: 'Serve!,' 'worship!,' 'devote yourselves in obedience!' — a command to render worship and humble service. The underlying sense is to submit oneself wholly, in reverence and obedience, to the one served.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group. The '-ū' ending means the order is given to several people: 'you all do it!' The initial vowel is a helping prosthetic vowel that lets the word begin, since the bare command stem would otherwise start with a vowelless letter.
7.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, devotion

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: "And hope for / expectantly await" — rajā is to hope with expectation: to look toward something desired as genuinely coming, combining hope and anticipation.
9.grammar: A plural imperative (command). Wa- joins it to a previous command ('and…'). The stem is the command form of 'to hope/expect'; the -ū ending addresses a group: 'you all, hope for / look forward to'. Commands take no tense ending — the form itself is the instruction.

10.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'the day,' very often used to mean 'today' or 'this day.' With the definite article it points to the present day as a defined, known span of time, and by extension can denote 'now' or 'the present moment.'
10.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending; on a noun of time it commonly marks it as an adverb answering 'when?' — fixing the action to that period ('on the day', 'today').
10.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

11.meaning: "The Last / the Final" — ākhir is what comes at the end; with 'the Day' it names the Last Day, the final Day toward which all things run.
11.grammar: An adjective made definite by al- 'the'. The final -a is the accusative ending: it typically marks the word as (or as describing) the object of a verb — an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes.
11.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, come after

12.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

13.meaning: A verb meaning to act with corruption, wreak havoc, or work mischief and ruin — to spread disorder and harm.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb directed at a plural 'you' (a group of males or a mixed group). The 'ta-' prefix signals 'you', and the -aw ending marks the plural 'you' subject. The vowelless (cut-off) form here is the mood used after certain particles, e.g. in prohibitions ('do not …').
13.root: ع-ث-و / ع-ث-ي (ʿ-th-w/y) — wreaking corruption and havoc

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
15.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

16.meaning: An active participle (the doer of an action) meaning 'corrupters', 'those who spread corruption' — people who cause ruin, disorder, and moral or social decay.
16.grammar: An active participle on the 'mu-' pattern, naming the one who performs the action of the related verb (to cause corruption). The -īna ending makes it a plural of males in the accusative or genitive case — the form used when the word is an object or otherwise governed, including as a circumstantial description ('… being corrupters').
16.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — corruption, spoiling, ruin

1.meaning: So they denied him / cried lies against him — a group rejected a single masculine figure as a liar, with a connector ('so/then') showing it follows as a consequence.
