12.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

13.meaning: He believes; he has faith. The verb denotes giving heartfelt trust and assent, especially affirming faith in Allah and what He has revealed; the form also carries the sense of granting security.
13.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he' for this verb pattern (form IV), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
13.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith, safety

14.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
14.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

16.meaning: denies / rejects
16.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form I (جَحَدَ), 3rd person masculine singular, indicative; meaning to deny despite knowing the truth
16.root: ج-ح-د (j-ḥ-d) — to deny, to repudiate, to disavow

17.meaning: 'With/in Our signs' — signs, tokens, proofs, or verses; the marks or revelations by which truth is shown. Combined with 'with/in' and 'our.'
17.grammar: The preposition 'bi' ('with/in/by') plus the feminine plural noun 'āyāt' ('signs/verses') plus the attached pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The '-i' is the genitive ending required after the preposition 'bi'; the noun is plural, and the whole phrase means '(connected) with our signs.'

18.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
18.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

19.meaning: Definite plural noun/participle: 'the disbelievers, those who reject faith' — those who cover over and deny the truth. The pattern names a whole group defined by this attribute.
19.grammar: A definite active participle ('the rejecters'). The '-ūna' ending is the masculine sound plural in the nominative (subject) case — the form a word takes when it is the doer of an action or the subject of a sentence ('the disbelievers [are/do]…').
19.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject, disbelieve

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

3.meaning: You all recite / they (fem.) recite — the present-tense act of reciting aloud, reading out, or rehearsing words in sequence (especially scripture), addressed to a male plural group ('you all') or done by a female plural subject ('they').
3.grammar: Present/imperfect tense. The 'ta-' prefix together with the '-ū' plural suffix marks either a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all recite') or a third-person feminine plural ('they recite'); a feminine singular reading is ruled out because the '-ū' suffix is plural. The ending '-ū' (without final 'na') is the shortened subjunctive/jussive mood, used after certain particles or in dependent clauses. The verb means 'recite/read out in sequence'.
3.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read out, follow in sequence

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
4.root: — (preposition)

5.meaning: Before; the period or point in time (or place) prior to something. With the attached pronoun it means 'before it / before him', pointing to what came earlier.
5.grammar: An adverb/noun of time meaning 'before', functioning here as something governed in the genitive (the -i ending), as it regularly follows a preposition such as 'from'. The attached -hi means 'it / him' ('before it'); the vowel of the pronoun is -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows the -i ending.
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede; front, priorness

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: A Book, a scripture — a written record or revealed text. In sacred usage it denotes a divinely revealed Scripture. The indefinite form means 'a book / some scripture' rather than a specific one.
7.grammar: A noun. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending: it marks the word as indefinite ('a book') and in the genitive case, the case typically used after a preposition or when one noun is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
7.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; 'kitāb' = something written, a book

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: "You write it (with your own hand)" — khaṭṭa is to draw lines, to trace script by hand; it is the root behind khaṭṭ, 'handwriting, calligraphy.'

parts.en: write, inscribe by hand (with -u present-tense ending)

9.grammar: Present-tense verb: ta- marks the subject "you" (masculine singular). The -u vowel after the doubled stem is the plain present (indicative) mood, a simple statement. The suffix -hu is the object pronoun "it/him": "you write it."

10.meaning: 'in/with your right hand': the right hand, often also implying strength, an oath, or a pledge. Addressed to a single male ('your').
10.grammar: A noun 'right hand' with the prefix bi- ('in/with/by means of') and the possessive -ka ('your', one male). Because bi- governs the genitive, the noun stands in that case (its -i vowel sits before the attached pronoun). The whole phrase means 'with/in your right hand'.
10.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right side/hand; also blessing, good fortune

11.meaning: In that case / then — a response particle signaling that what follows is the consequence of a just-stated condition or supposition ('if so, then…').
11.grammar: A response/consequence particle, not a noun or verb. The -an ending is a fixed part of the word (written with a final alif), not a live grammatical case. It introduces the result side of a hypothetical ('then you would…').

12.meaning: "(Then) surely (he/they) would have doubted" — irtāba is to fall into doubt, to let inner disquiet and suspicion take hold of oneself.

parts.en: then surely (introduces the result of an 'if')

12.grammar: The la- prefix is the particle that opens the answer to a hypothetical "if" clause: "(had such-and-such been) … then surely …" The verb is past tense, and its final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("he" — or a collective). It is Form VIII, an inward-turning pattern: not just "doubt" but "take doubt into oneself, become doubtful."

13.meaning: Those who pursue falsehood / the perpetrators of vanity — people who deal in what is false, baseless, or futile, or who try to nullify the truth.
13.grammar: A definite active participle (the doer) from the causative pattern, naming those who engage in falsehood or seek to invalidate truth. The '-ūna' ending marks the masculine plural in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
13.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — falsehood, vanity, to be null/void

1.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

2.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
2.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

3.meaning: "signs / verses / tokens" — the plural of āya, a 'sign' or evident token that points to something beyond itself; it also denotes a verse of revelation, each one a sign.
3.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -u is the nominative case, the form taken as the subject of a sentence or the leading term of a possessive chain ('the signs OF …').

4.meaning: Clear proofs, plain signs, manifest evidences — things so evident they make the truth obvious and leave no ambiguity.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun. The '-un' ending is nominative and indefinite: the nominative case typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('clear proofs'). It is the plural of a word meaning 'clear/manifest'.
4.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness, to make plain

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: "the breasts / chests (of)" — plural of ṣadr, the chest; in Qur'anic idiom the breast is the seat of thoughts, feelings, and secrets, so 'what the breasts contain' means people's innermost selves.
6.grammar: A broken (internal) plural of ṣadr. The -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the breasts OF ...') or follows a preposition. The missing tanwīn confirms it stands in such an 'of' construction.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
8.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
8.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

9.meaning: Knowledge — sure, established awareness and understanding of how things truly are, as opposed to ignorance, guesswork, or mere opinion.
9.grammar: A definite noun ('the knowledge'). The -a ending marks the accusative case, which most often signals that the noun is the direct object of a verb (the thing being received or acted upon) or otherwise governed into that case.
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, sure awareness

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: denies / rejects
11.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form I (جَحَدَ), 3rd person masculine singular, indicative; meaning to deny despite knowing the truth
11.root: ج-ح-د (j-ḥ-d) — to deny, to repudiate, to disavow

12.meaning: 'With/in Our signs' — signs, tokens, proofs, or verses; the marks or revelations by which truth is shown. Combined with 'with/in' and 'our.'
12.grammar: The preposition 'bi' ('with/in/by') plus the feminine plural noun 'āyāt' ('signs/verses') plus the attached pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The '-i' is the genitive ending required after the preposition 'bi'; the noun is plural, and the whole phrase means '(connected) with our signs.'

13.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
13.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
13.root: — (particle)

14.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
14.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
2.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

3.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
3.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
3.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

4.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
4.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

5.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evidences; also the discrete verses of revelation. Each is a clear indicator pointing to a greater truth or to its divine source.
5.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun. The ending -tun consists of the feminine plural marker -āt together with the nominative case (used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing who/what something is) and nunation (the -n sound) marking it as indefinite ('signs', not 'the signs').

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'his Lord'. 'Lord' (rabb) denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs — far richer than a mere title; here joined to 'his'.
7.grammar: The noun 'Lord' with the genitive -i ending followed by the attached pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive case appears because the noun is linked to a preceding word ('… OF his Lord') or follows a preposition. The lengthened -hī reflects how this pronoun is pronounced after an -i vowel.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, ownership, sustaining and bringing to completion

8.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
8.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

9.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
9.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

10.meaning: the signs / the clear tokens, evidences, or verses. The plural of a word meaning a sign that points to a truth — a marker, proof, or miracle; also a verse of revelation.
10.grammar: A feminine plural noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The -u ending typically marks the nominative case — the subject of a sentence or the thing being named/identified.
10.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark, evidence

11.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
11.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: And only / and indeed it is merely — a particle combination that restricts and emphasizes, conveying 'and it is nothing but ...' or 'and the only thing is ...'.
13.grammar: A compound particle: 'wa' (and) + the emphatic 'inna' (truly/indeed) fused with 'mā'. Together 'innamā' functions as a restriction marker meaning 'only / nothing but ...', limiting the statement to what follows and asserting it emphatically.

14.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
14.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

15.meaning: A warner — one who gives warning, alerting people to impending danger or consequence so they may take heed. It names the agent who delivers such an admonition.
15.grammar: A noun/adjective on the intensive agent-pattern (faʿīl), denoting one who does something fully or by office — a 'warner'. The ending -un is nominative and indefinite ('a warner'); the nominative marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate, so this typically stands as 'is a warner' or 'a warner (came)'.
15.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice of danger

16.meaning: Clear, plain, and self-evident; that which makes things manifest. The form carries an active sense: not merely 'clear in itself' but 'making clear,' something that openly displays its nature and leaves no ambiguity.
16.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) on the form mufʿil, meaning 'one who/that which makes [something] clear.' The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending ('a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.
16.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinctness, clarity

1.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
1.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').

2.meaning: "It suffices them / is enough for them" — kafā is to be sufficient, to meet a need fully so that nothing more is required.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb with ya- = "it/he." The stem ends in a short -i where the verb's full form would have a long -ī (yakfī): that clipped final vowel is the mark of the jussive mood, the shortened form a verb takes after particles such as "did not," "let," or a rhetorical "has it not…?" The suffix -him is the object pronoun "them."

3.meaning: That We … — an emphatic linking particle 'that' fused with the pronoun 'We.' 'Anna' introduces and asserts a fact ('that indeed …'), and the attached 'We' names the doer (a majestic or plural 'We').
3.grammar: An emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -nā 'we.' This family of particles takes a following noun/pronoun in the accusative as its subject, so -nā here functions as that subject: 'that We …'. It firmly introduces a stated fact.

4.meaning: We sent down — to cause something to descend or be revealed from a higher source to a lower; classically used of revelation sent down from on high.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative (fourth) form, meaning to make something come down. The attached -nā is the subject pronoun 'we', marking the action as completed and done by a 'we' (a form of majestic/collective speech when used of Allah).
4.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, be sent down

5.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

6.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
6.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
6.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

7.meaning: It is recited / read aloud — a passage of revelation is being conveyed by being read out.
7.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is being recited'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive (no doer named), and the final weak -ā shows it derives from a root ending in a weak letter; it conveys an ongoing action done to the subject.
7.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
8.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
8.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
9.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
11.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

12.meaning: "Surely a mercy" — raḥma is mercy: tender, protective compassion that moves one to do good to another; the womb-like care from which the word itself grows.
12.grammar: la- is the emphatic particle "surely." The ending -an (written as doubled fatḥa, pronounced with the feminine -t-) is the indefinite accusative: the -n sound means "a" (not "the"). This is the shape a noun takes as the subject of an emphatic "indeed…"-type (inna) sentence — inna puts its subject-noun in the accusative. When a phrase like "in that (is)…" comes first as the statement's predicate, the subject-noun follows it, and the emphatic la- then attaches directly to that delayed subject: "(in that is) surely A mercy."

13.meaning: A reminder, remembrance, or admonition — something that calls a truth back to mind. The feminine form often denotes the act or means of reminding, a lesson or warning that prompts recollection.
13.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and', joining this to what precedes. The word ends in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra); nouns of this pattern do not change their ending for case, so the -ā simply marks the feminine noun-form and stays the same whether subject, object, or possessed.
13.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention

14.meaning: 'For a people / for a folk' — directed toward a community or group of human beings considered collectively.
14.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a noun 'people.' Because it follows a preposition, the noun takes the genitive, and the tanwīn (the -in ending) marks it as indefinite ('a people'). The whole phrase means 'for a people,' directing something toward that group.
14.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

15.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
15.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: "he/it sufficed" or "enough is …" — to be adequate and to spare, leaving no need for anything more. Used to declare that something or someone fully meets the need.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb from a root ending in a weak letter, so its final syllable appears as a long -ā. It reports a single completed action and, by its bare masculine form, takes "he/it" as subject. It commonly carries the sense "X is enough / X suffices."

3.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
3.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

4.meaning: 'Between me' — the spatial or relational word 'between' joined to 'me'. It marks the point or interval that lies on the speaker's side of a relationship between two parties.
4.grammar: The adverb/noun 'between' with the attached pronoun 'me'. 'Between' takes a following word in the genitive (linked-to) relation, and the -ī ending is the attached pronoun meaning 'me/my'.
4.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

5.meaning: 'And between you' — the word for 'between/among' joined by 'and', with 'you (all)' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between you.
5.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the adverb of place 'between' (fixed in the -a form), with the attached pronoun -kum ('you', masculine plural). Together they mean 'and between you (all)', marking a relation involving the addressees.
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

6.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
6.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.

7.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
7.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
7.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
10.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

11.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
11.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

12.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
13.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
13.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

14.meaning: With / by falsehood — 'the false, the vain, the baseless' joined to a preposition and 'the'.
14.grammar: The preposition bi- joined to the definite noun 'the falsehood' (an active participle meaning 'that which is null/vain'). The -i ending is the genitive, required because the noun follows the preposition.
14.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be void, false, vain, of no effect

15.meaning: And they disbelieved, they rejected the truth — a past act of a group covering over and denying faith, or being ungrateful.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb with a plural subject. The prefix wa- means 'and'. The ending -ū means 'they' for a masculine group and shows the action is completed (past). The written alif after the -ū is silent and is simply the spelling convention for this plural ending.
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, reject, be ungrateful

16.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
16.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
16.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

17.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
17.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

18.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
18.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

19.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'the losers' or 'those who suffer loss' — people who end up in ruin, having forfeited what is of true value.
19.grammar: Definite plural noun (active participle in form) with the article al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine 'sound' plural in the nominative case (the form used for a subject or predicate). The participle names the agent: 'those who incur loss'.
19.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose, suffer loss, be ruined

1.meaning: 'and they seek to hasten you / they ask you to bring it on quickly' — they press for something to be brought about sooner, demanding it be rushed.

parts.en: they seek to hasten / demand the hastening of

1.grammar: A present-tense verb in form X (the ist- pattern often means 'to seek/ask for' the action of the root), so 'to seek the hastening of'. The ya-…-ūna frame marks third-person masculine plural 'they'. The -ūna ending is the indicative mood, the verb's normal/affirmative form. The final -ka is the attached object pronoun 'you' (masculine singular). The wa- prefix means 'and'.

2.meaning: With the punishment — bil-ʿadhābi is bi- (with, by) plus al-ʿadhāb (the punishment, the torment, the chastisement).

parts.en: preposition with definite article: with the, by the
noun, definite genitive: the punishment, the torment, the chastisement

2.grammar: Bil- is bi- + al- (the definite article assimilates to the following letter if it is a 'sun letter'; here ʿayn is a 'moon letter' so it stays al-). ʿAdhābi is the genitive (kasra -i) following the preposition bi-.
2.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, to torment; punishment, chastisement

3.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

3.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

4.meaning: 'A term / appointed time / fixed span' — 'ajal' is a set period or the deadline at its end; the appointed time fixed for something to occur or end. Indefinite ('a term').
4.grammar: A noun with the ending '-un' (nunation), which marks it as indefinite ('a term') and in the nominative case — the form used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.
4.root: ا-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed time

5.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'named, specified, designated, made definite.' It describes something that has been clearly stated and fixed by name — a term that is precisely set rather than vague.
5.grammar: A passive participle (the mu- prefix forms a 'one that is …' word from the Form II intensive pattern, with a doubled middle root letter) meaning 'named/specified.' It carries the indefinite ending -an, written with alif maqṣūra (a final ya-shaped letter sounded as -ā). Because it ends in this weak final letter, the form stays the same whether nominative, accusative, or genitive — context shows it is describing an indefinite noun.
5.root: س-م-ي (s-m-y) — name, naming; to give or assign a name

6.meaning: "Surely (it) would have come to them" — jāʾa is the plain verb of arrival: to come, to reach someone.

parts.en: then surely (introduces the result of an 'if')

6.grammar: la- is the particle that opens the answer of a hypothetical "if … then surely …" sentence. The verb is past tense, third-person masculine singular ("it/he came"). The suffix -hum is the object pronoun "them"; the extra -u at its end is only a helper vowel that eases the join to a following word beginning with a joined (unvowelled) letter.

7.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
7.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.

8.meaning: "And it shall most surely come to them" — a doubly-emphasized promise of arrival: not merely "it will come" but a solemn oath-strength "it shall without any doubt come."
8.grammar: The frame la- … -nna wrapped around a present-tense verb is Arabic's strongest future assertion, the form used in oaths: "it SHALL most certainly …" The ya- prefix marks the subject "it/he." Before the emphatic -nna the verb's final vowel becomes -a. The suffix -hum is the object pronoun "them."

9.meaning: An adverb meaning 'suddenly, all at once, unexpectedly' — something arriving abruptly without warning.

parts.en: accusative ending with nunation, here forming an adverb

9.grammar: A noun in the accusative case with nunation (the -an ending, the doubled final 'n' sound). This accusative-with-nunation pattern characteristically turns a noun into an adverb of manner — answering 'how?' with 'suddenly.'
9.root: ب-غ-ت (b-gh-t) — to come suddenly, take by surprise

10.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
10.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'they perceive / they are aware / they sense.' The root denotes fine, immediate awareness — noticing or feeling something, often subconsciously. It frequently appears in the negative, expressing that people fail to realize something.

parts.en: perceive / sense / be aware (Form I stem)

12.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, Form I (imperfect stem yashʿuru, with -u- after the second root letter), third-person masculine plural. The prefix 'ya-' and ending -ūna give 'they (masc.) do / are doing,' the -ūna marking the indicative — an ongoing or habitual state of awareness (or, when negated, the lack of it).
12.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to perceive, sense, be finely aware

1.meaning: "They ask you to hasten (it) / demand that you hurry it along" — istaʿjala is to seek speed: to press impatiently for something to be brought on sooner.
1.grammar: Present-tense verb in Form X, whose sta- element — prefixed in front of all three root letters — means "to seek or demand" the root idea: here, to seek haste. ya- plus the -ūna ending together mark a plural "they," and the retained -na shows the plain statement (indicative) mood. The final -ka is the object pronoun "you" (one man): "they press YOU for haste."

2.meaning: With the punishment — bil-ʿadhābi is bi- (with, by) plus al-ʿadhāb (the punishment, the torment, the chastisement).

parts.en: preposition with definite article: with the, by the
noun, definite genitive: the punishment, the torment, the chastisement

2.grammar: Bil- is bi- + al- (the definite article assimilates to the following letter if it is a 'sun letter'; here ʿayn is a 'moon letter' so it stays al-). ʿAdhābi is the genitive (kasra -i) following the preposition bi-.
2.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, to torment; punishment, chastisement

3.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
3.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

4.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
4.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
4.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

5.meaning: An active participle (a doer-noun) meaning 'surely encompassing / encircling / surrounding on all sides' — that which closes in around something completely, leaving no escape. Carries a leading emphatic 'surely'.
5.grammar: An active participle in the feminine singular, naming that which does the action: 'one that encompasses'. The ending -un (with nunation) is the nominative case with no definite article, typically marking an indefinite subject or predicate ('a surrounding thing'). The prefixed la- adds emphasis, 'surely'.

6.meaning: 'of / with the disbelievers' — the preposition 'with/of' joined to 'the disbelievers', those who reject faith and cover over the truth.
6.grammar: A preposition plus a definite plural noun. bi- attaches a word to a verb or participle (here 'with/over'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in the genitive/accusative form, required because the noun follows a preposition; it means 'the (male) ones who disbelieve'.
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject, disbelieve

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: "It envelops them / covers them over" — ghashiya is to cover, veil, or overwhelm something so that it is wrapped on every side, as a blanket or an engulfing cloud.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb: ya- marks the subject "it/he." The -ā before the pronoun is the verb's own weak final letter, which absorbs the usual present-tense case vowel. The suffix -hum is the object pronoun "them," and its final -u is only a helper vowel smoothing the link to a following word.

3.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
3.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
4.root: — (preposition)

5.meaning: Above them / over them — the place or position over the top of someone or something, joined to 'them'.
5.grammar: A noun of place meaning 'above/over,' commonly used to mean 'over …'. The -i (kasra) is the genitive ending, here triggered by the following possessor; the attached '-him' is 'them' (its vowel is 'hi' after an -i sound).
5.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above; aboveness, superiority

6.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
6.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

7.meaning: Beneath / under — the place or position below something. Often paired with imagery of rivers flowing 'beneath'.
7.grammar: A frozen adverbial noun of place meaning 'under/below,' normally linked to a following noun ('beneath …'). It is not derived from a verb. The final -i (kasra) is the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or as the first term tied to a following noun.
7.root: تَحۡت (taḥt) — a frozen adverb of place ('below/beneath'); not derived from a trilateral verbal root

8.meaning: Their feet / their legs — the foot (or leg), here joined to 'their'.
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'rijl' (foot/leg). The -i (kasra) is the genitive ending, here because a possessor follows; the attached '-him' is 'their' (its vowel is 'hi' after an -i sound).
8.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — foot, leg; to go on foot

9.meaning: And he says, and he will say. A verb of speaking covering plain statement, and by extension holding an opinion or asking.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb for a single male ('he says/will say'), joined by wa- ('and'). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain statement of fact (ongoing or future) rather than a command or a 'so that' clause.

10.meaning: Taste! / experience it firsthand — a command to undergo and feel something directly, as one tastes food. Often used of being made to feel a consequence.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group: 'taste!' The -ū ending marks the addressee as masculine plural ('you all'). From a hollow root whose middle letter appears as a long ū in this form.
10.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience directly

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
12.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. As the doer is built into the suffix, the verb itself is in its base past form ('you all were').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

13.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
13.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: O My slaves — yāʿibādiya is a vocative meaning 'O My servants/slaves', directly addressing the believers with divine intimacy.

parts.en: My servants, My slaves (plural with first person possessive yāʾ)

1.grammar: Yā is the vocative particle. ʿIbādiya is the broken plural of ʿabd with the first-person possessive yāʾ (ʿibādī in full form, ʿibādiya with full yāʾ in this instance). This is from the famous 'Qul yā ʿibādiya alladhīna asrafū ʿalā anfusihim' — the divine proclamation of mercy to those who have transgressed.
1.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, to worship; slave, servant

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They believed, they came to faith; to place trust and security in something and affirm it as true (the inner act of faith).
3.grammar: A past-tense verb of the Form IV (causative) pattern. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') for a completed action ('they believed'). The final written alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
4.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

5.meaning: "My earth / My land" — arḍ is the earth, ground, or land; with the possessive it is "My earth," spoken by its Owner of the wide world He has made.
5.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -ī, which simply means "my." This "my" swallows the noun's own case vowel, so the same written form serves whatever role the word plays; the pronoun also makes the noun definite — a possessed noun never takes "the" or the indefinite -n.

6.meaning: Spacious, vast, wide-reaching — describing something (feminine) that has ample room or extent, with the sense of encompassing breadth rather than narrowness.
6.grammar: An active participle ('one that is spacious') in the feminine. The -at marks feminine agreement with a feminine noun it describes. The final -un is the nominative indefinite ending: -u signals the subject/predicate case (the word is the doer or the statement's main topic), and the added -n (tanwīn) means 'a/any', i.e. indefinite.
6.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — to be wide, spacious, to encompass

7.meaning: A connective 'so / and' joined to an emphatic, isolated object pronoun meaning 'Me alone / Me in particular.' The special form 'iyyā-' with an attached pronoun singles out the object for exclusive emphasis ('it is Me, and none else').
7.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' means 'so / then.' 'Iyyā' is a special carrier used to put an object pronoun first for emphasis or exclusivity; the attached '-ya' is the first-person singular pronoun 'me.' Fronting an object this way typically conveys 'Me alone / it is Me specifically.'

8.meaning: 'So worship Me / therefore serve Me (alone).' A command to render worship — humble service, obedience, and devotion — directed to the single speaker. The verb implies total submission and exclusive devotion to the one commanding.

parts.en: imperative base 'worship!' (helping vowel u- + bare stem)

8.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group ('you all worship'), shown by the -ū plural ending. The base uʿ'bud- is the bare imperative stem: it opens with a helping vowel u- (needed because the stem otherwise begins with a cluster) and carries no thematic vowel of its own — distinguishing it from the indicative yaʿbudu. The leading fa- means 'so/therefore,' linking the order to a preceding reason, and the final -ni attaches the object pronoun 'Me,' so the whole is 'so worship Me.' Being an imperative, it gives an instruction rather than stating a fact.
8.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit in devotion

1.meaning: A quantifying noun meaning 'each', 'every', or 'all'. When joined to a following noun it sweeps that noun up in its entirety or distributes over every instance of it ('every man', 'all of it'); it expresses totality or comprehensiveness.
1.grammar: A noun used to quantify. The final -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as standing independently. It is normally placed before a noun in the genitive ('all OF …', 'every …').

2.meaning: A noun meaning 'soul, self, person, living being.' It denotes the inner self or the whole individual — the seat of life and identity, and by extension a 'person' as a single unit.
2.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a soul'). This form appears after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun (such as 'every soul').
2.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being

3.meaning: One who tastes / is going to taste — the doer of tasting; one who experiences something by tasting it. Often used figuratively for undergoing or experiencing.
3.grammar: An active participle ('one tasting') in the feminine form. The tāʾ marbūṭa 'ة' carries the feminine marker, and the ḍamma on it ('-atu') is the nominative case vowel — the two belong to one ending and are not separate morphemes. The nominative signals the word functions as a subject or describes one; as a participle it can govern a following noun like a verb governs its object.

4.meaning: 'death' — the cessation of life; the state or event of dying.
4.grammar: A definite singular noun. The al- is 'the'; the -i ending is genitive, used after a preposition or to link this word to a preceding noun in a possessive '… of death' relationship.
4.root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) — to die; death

5.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
5.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

6.meaning: 'To us / toward us' — the preposition 'to/toward' joined to the pronoun 'us,' expressing direction or motion toward the speakers.
6.grammar: Preposition 'ilā' (to/toward), which shifts to the form 'ilay-' before a pronoun, plus the attached pronoun -nā, 'us.' Pronouns after a preposition stand in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -nā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

7.meaning: 'You are returned / brought back' — a passive verb from the root meaning to return: the subjects are made to go back, sent back to a point of origin, the action being done to them rather than by them.
7.grammar: Present/future passive. The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the internal vowelling (u–a) makes it passive — the action is done TO the subject. The -ūna ending is the full ('indicative') plural form, used when the verb is not cut short by certain particles.

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
3.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

4.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
4.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
4.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

5.meaning: An emphatic promise: 'We will most certainly settle them / give them a dwelling-place / establish them,' with an attached pronoun 'them.' It speaks of granting a secure place or standing.
5.grammar: The opening 'la-' is an emphatic particle ('surely, certainly'). The 'nu-' prefix marks the doer as 'we.' This is a Form II verb (the doubled-middle pattern, often intensive/causative: 'to settle someone'). The doubled '-nna' is the heavy emphatic ending that strengthens a promise or threat; the final '-hum' is the attached object pronoun 'them.'
5.root: ب-و-أ (b-w-') — to settle in a place, take up a dwelling, give an abode

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
7.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
7.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

8.meaning: Lofty chambers, upper rooms — plural of ghurfah, an elevated room or high dwelling; in Qur'anic usage it evokes the exalted dwellings of Paradise.
8.grammar: A broken (internal) plural of ghurfah — Arabic often pluralizes by reshaping the word's vowels rather than adding a suffix. The final -an is the accusative indefinite ending: -a is the case used for a direct object (the thing acted upon), and the -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('lofty chambers', not 'the chambers').
8.root: غ-ر-ف (gh-r-f) — to scoop up; hence a raised chamber, an upper room

9.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
11.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

12.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
12.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

13.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
13.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.
13.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — perpetuity, everlasting abiding

14.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
14.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

15.meaning: How excellent! How good! A fixed verb of praise used to declare that something is outstandingly good. It is not an ordinary action verb but a formula that lavishes commendation on whatever follows it.

parts.en: how excellent is / what a good

15.grammar: A frozen verb of praise. It does not inflect for ordinary tense; it stands at the head of a statement to commend the noun that comes after it as supremely good. The closing -a is part of its fixed form rather than a productive case ending.

16.meaning: Reward, recompense, wage — the return or compensation given for what one has done; payment for work or deeds.
16.grammar: A noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, as here without nunation, a noun that is the first term of a possessive phrase ('the reward of …'). It denotes a deserved recompense, whether worldly or in the Hereafter.
16.root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — to recompense, reward; wages, reward

17.meaning: The doers / the workers — those who act and put things into practice, especially the ones who do righteous deeds. The word names people defined by their working and acting.
17.grammar: An active participle in the sound masculine plural, made definite by 'al-'. The '-īna' ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural, meaning 'the ones who…'; here it typically follows a possessive link ('the reward of the workers'). It denotes habitual doers — those characterized by working and acting.
17.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deed, work

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: 'They were patient / they endured steadfastly / they persevered.' The verb means to restrain oneself, to bear hardship with calm endurance, to hold firm and not give way to panic or complaint. Ṣabr is steadfast, self-controlled perseverance.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form I) in the masculine plural 'they' person. The stem ṣabar- carries the completed-action (past) sense. The -ū ending marks the doers as 'they' (masculine plural) who performed the act ('they were patient / they endured'). The written alif after it is a silent spelling convention that regularly follows the plural -ū on a verb and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: A compound, 'and upon / and on / and against' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, against'). It adds a further thing onto which something rests or against which it bears.
3.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and', joining what follows to what came before. ʿalā is an indeclinable preposition that puts the following noun in the genitive case and signals 'on, over, or upon' something.

4.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
4.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

5.meaning: They place their reliance and trust, committing their affairs to another and depending wholly upon Him. Conveys active, ongoing dependence and entrusting of outcomes.
5.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb from Form V (reflexive: 'to make oneself rely'). The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject doing the action now or habitually ('they rely'). The -na also signals the verb is in its full, uninterrupted form.
5.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, appoint as guardian, rely upon; committing one's affairs to another.

1.meaning: 'And how many…!' — an expression of multitude meaning 'how many a…' or 'so many a…', used to marvel at a large, indefinite number.
1.grammar: 'Wa-' ('and') plus the compound particle 'ka-ayyin', which means 'how many' / 'many a'. It is a quantity word expressing an indefinite large number and is normally followed by 'min' plus a singular noun. It does not itself take a case ending.

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

3.meaning: A moving creature, a living thing that treads or walks the earth; any animal that moves of its own accord.
3.grammar: An indefinite singular feminine noun ('a creature'); the -at- syllable is the feminine marker. The -in ending (nunation) signals indefiniteness and is the genitive case, taken after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage.
3.root: د-ب-ب (d-b-b) — to move/creep along, to tread the ground

4.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
4.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

5.meaning: 'she/it carries / bears / is pregnant with' — to hold, bear, or carry a load, including bearing a child.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix here marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it'). The -u ending marks the indicative mood, the verb's normal affirmative form ('she carries').
5.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, bear, be pregnant

6.meaning: Its provision — rizq is sustenance in the widest sense: food, livelihood, every means of life that Allah allots to a creature; with 'its/her' attached, the provision belonging to that creature.
6.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as a direct object — the thing carried, given, or acted upon. The suffix -hā means 'its/her' (referring back to something grammatically feminine, such as a creature), so the whole means 'its provision'.
6.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, to grant sustenance

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

8.meaning: He provides for it — an ongoing act of giving sustenance: He (Allah) continually supplies that creature with what it needs to live.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix means 'he' — a masculine singular subject doing the action now or habitually. The -u vowel after the stem is the indicative mood marker: it signals a plain statement of ongoing/repeated fact ('he provides', 'he keeps providing'). The suffix -hā is the object 'it/her' — the one receiving the provision.
8.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, to grant sustenance

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and you (plural)' used as a standalone object — 'and you yourselves.' The base iyyā- is a special particle that carries an object pronoun when it cannot attach directly to a verb, here with 'you all.'
9.grammar: A connective 'and' joined to a detached object pronoun. The element iyyā- exists precisely to bear an object pronoun in isolation (when it cannot be suffixed onto a verb); the attached -kum means 'you all' (masculine plural) and functions as the object.

10.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
10.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

11.meaning: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
11.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

12.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
12.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

2.meaning: To ask, question, or request — to put a query to someone or seek something from them. With the endings attached it means 'you asked them,' a completed act of questioning directed at a group.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action. The suffix -ta marks the doer as second-person masculine singular ('you'); the further suffix -hum is the direct object 'them.'

3.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
