3.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

4.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
4.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.
4.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — creating, originating, shaping

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

6.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
6.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.

7.meaning: And He made (something) subservient, harnessed it, or pressed it into service — to bring a thing under control so it works toward an appointed purpose.
7.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The verb is past tense for 'he' (third-person masculine singular); its doubled middle letter marks an intensive/causative pattern ('to make subservient'), and the -a ending is the standard past-tense vowel for a single masculine doer who completed the act.
7.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to subject, subdue, press into service

8.meaning: The sun — the blazing daytime luminary.
8.grammar: A feminine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.

9.meaning: The moon — the luminous body of the night sky that waxes and wanes.
9.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus the definite noun with article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative case, which commonly marks the word as the object of a verb — the thing acted upon, placed, or appointed.

10.meaning: An emphatic assertion 'they will surely say / they will certainly say.' The word fuses an oath-like emphasis with a future statement of speaking, leaving no doubt that the utterance will occur. The heavy doubled ending drives home the certainty.
10.grammar: A present/future verb made doubly emphatic. The opening la- means 'surely'; the ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine subject; and the heavy -nna suffix (the 'energetic' ending) intensifies it to 'they will most certainly say.' Together la-…-nna is a fixed pattern of strong affirmation about something yet to happen.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: An interrogative of manner or place meaning 'how?', 'in what way?', or 'whence / from where?'. It expresses wonder or challenge at how something could be so, often implying 'how on earth…?'.
12.grammar: A connective 'fa' ('so/then') joined to an indeclinable question-word. Being a fixed particle, it has no case ending; it opens a question about manner or source and carries a tone of astonishment or rebuke.

13.meaning: They are turned away / deluded — a passive verb meaning that people are diverted away from truth toward falsehood, made to deviate from what is right.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice — the u- prefix vowel with an a-vowel on the stem signals 'are being [acted upon]', so the subjects are the ones turned away, not the ones turning. The -ūna ending marks a 3rd-person masculine plural subject ('they') and the indicative mood (a plain statement). The sense is being led astray or deluded away from the truth.
13.root: ا-ف-ك (ʾ-f-k) — turning away, deviation, falsehood and deception

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: He spreads out, extends, stretches forth, and makes ample. The verb conveys laying something open and wide, and so giving abundantly or enlarging a provision.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; the 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' marks the plain indicative — an ongoing or habitual action ('he extends / keeps extending'). The root pictures spreading a thing out flat and wide, hence giving generously.
2.root: ب-س-ط (b-s-ṭ) — spreading out, extending, expanding, making ample

3.meaning: The provision; sustenance, livelihood, and the means of life — whatever bounty is granted to support and nourish a creature, whether food, wealth, or any good thing bestowed.
3.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the'; its 'r' doubles the sun-letter assimilation of the 'l'). It is a verbal noun on the 'fiʿl' pattern denoting that which is provided. The final '-a' is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing given or acted upon).
3.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, bestowing the means of life

4.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
4.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

5.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
5.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
5.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: 'His servants / His slaves / His worshippers' — ʿibād are those who serve and worship; with the attached pronoun it denotes the servants belonging to Him (Allah), i.e., humankind or His devotees.
7.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel is the genitive case, typically appearing after a preposition or in a possessive ('of') link; the pronoun names the one to whom the servants belong.

8.meaning: And He measures out, restricts, straitens, or apportions sparingly; to set a fixed measure to provision so as to limit it. The same verb can also mean to have power and to determine.
8.grammar: The prefix 'wa' means 'and'. The core is a present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; 'ya-' marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' marks the plain indicative — an ongoing or habitual action ('he restricts / keeps measuring out'). The root joins the ideas of measuring, decreeing, and having power.

9.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
9.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
12.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

13.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
13.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
13.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

14.meaning: 'All-Knowing / deeply knowledgeable' — an intensive adjective from the root for knowledge, describing one whose knowledge is vast and complete; when applied in the highest sense it means perfectly and comprehensively knowing all things.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun of the 'faʿīl' pattern, expressing an abundant, deep-seated quality ('one who knows thoroughly'). The final -un is the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (nunation) and indefiniteness — the nominative is the basic 'subject / predicate' state, and the doubled-n sound marks it as indefinite ('(an) all-knowing one').

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

2.meaning: To ask, question, or request — to put a query to someone or seek something from them. With the endings attached it means 'you asked them,' a completed act of questioning directed at a group.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action. The suffix -ta marks the doer as second-person masculine singular ('you'); the further suffix -hum is the direct object 'them.'

3.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

4.meaning: He sent down — the doubled middle letter (Form II) adds intensity or repetition: to send down again and again, in stages or in abundance; used of rain and of revelation descending from Allah.

parts.en: sent down (intensive stem: repeatedly / in stages)

4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the intensive Form II pattern — the doubled z conveys sending down repeatedly or in portions, not just once. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he': it tells you a masculine singular subject completed the action ('he sent down').
4.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, to come down

5.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
5.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

6.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
6.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

7.meaning: 'water' — water in general, the fluid essential to life; also used for liquid such as rain. A basic noun for the substance of water.
7.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case together with indefiniteness — commonly the role of a direct object, the thing acted upon (e.g. what is sent down or brought).

8.meaning: And so He gave life, revived, brought to life what was lifeless; the causative sense 'to make alive'.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb introduced by 'fa' ('and so / then', often signalling a result or sequence). The verb is third-person masculine singular ('he gave life'); the prefixed 'a' belongs to the causative (Form IV) pattern, turning 'to live' into 'to give life'.

9.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

10.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
10.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
12.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
12.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

13.meaning: Its death, its lifelessness or dormancy; the state of being dead, joined to a possessor.
13.grammar: A noun ('death') with an attached third-person feminine singular possessive pronoun ('its / her'). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, the case taken before a possessor pronoun and after prepositions ('death of it').
13.root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) — death, to die

14.meaning: An emphatic assertion 'they will surely say / they will certainly say.' The word fuses an oath-like emphasis with a future statement of speaking, leaving no doubt that the utterance will occur. The heavy doubled ending drives home the certainty.
14.grammar: A present/future verb made doubly emphatic. The opening la- means 'surely'; the ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine subject; and the heavy -nna suffix (the 'energetic' ending) intensifies it to 'they will most certainly say.' Together la-…-nna is a fixed pattern of strong affirmation about something yet to happen.

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
16.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.
16.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak

17.meaning: All praise, commendation, and grateful acknowledgement — the recognition that beauty, goodness, and perfection rightly belong to and are owed to the one being praised. As a definite noun with the article 'al-', it conveys that the totality of praise is encompassed.
17.grammar: A definite noun (carrying the article 'al-', 'the'). The final '-u' ending is nominative: it marks the word as the subject or main topic of a statement — the thing being talked about or the doer of an action, rather than its object.
17.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise, to commend, to give thanks

18.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
18.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

19.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
19.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

20.meaning: Most of them / the greater part of them — the noun 'akthar' (the greater number, the majority), built on a comparative/superlative pattern of k-th-r ('much/many'), with the pronoun 'them'.
20.grammar: A noun in possessive (genitive) construction: 'aktharu' ('the most of') plus the attached pronoun '-hum' ('them') yields 'most of them'. The '-u' on 'akthar' is the nominative ending, typical when this phrase serves as the subject.
20.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, numerous

21.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
21.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

22.meaning: They use their reason, they understand and reflect; to grasp things with the intellect and restrain oneself accordingly.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -na ending also signals the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action ('they use reason').
22.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand; to restrain (as a tether restrains)

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

3.meaning: 'The life' — earthly existence, the span of living in this world. The word denotes life as the state of being alive, vitality, and the worldly life as a whole.
3.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the'. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something), or as the predicate naming what something is.

4.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
4.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
4.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

6.meaning: Diversion, amusement — lahw is pastime that distracts the heart from what truly matters; idle entertainment that occupies without lasting benefit.
6.grammar: A simple noun. The -un ending is nominative indefinite: the -u marks the subject/predicate case — the word names what something is or what is being talked about — and the -n (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness ('a diversion', 'mere diversion').
6.root: ل-ه-و (l-h-w) — to be diverted, distracted by amusement

7.meaning: And play — laʿib is play or sport: activity done for fun without serious purpose or lasting outcome; joined by 'and' to what precedes it.
7.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connector 'and', linking this noun to a preceding one. The -un ending is nominative indefinite: -u for the subject/predicate case (matching the word it is paired with) and -n (tanwīn) for indefiniteness ('play' in general, not a specific instance).

8.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
8.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

9.meaning: the home / the Abode (of the Hereafter). Al-dār refers to a home or abode — here specifically al-dār al-ākhira, the Abode of the Hereafter, the final and ultimate dwelling.
9.grammar: Feminine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), -a (fatḥa) ending. Object of the preceding verb.
9.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to circle; dār: home, abode, dwelling

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come' — literally 'the last (abode)', the final, everlasting existence following this present life.
10.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the') bearing the -a ending, which marks the accusative (object) case — the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb. It is feminine in form (the tā' marbūṭa ending).
10.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; lastness, the end

11.meaning: Surely it — an emphatic particle fused to the pronoun 'it/she': la- adds strong affirmation ('truly, indeed'), and hiya points to a feminine subject about to be identified or described.
11.grammar: The la- is the emphatic lām: it does not translate to a separate word so much as underline the whole statement — 'it truly is…'. Hiya is the independent pronoun 'she/it' used for feminine nouns; as a pronoun it has no case ending, and it typically stands as the subject of a statement of identity ('it is …').

12.meaning: The (true) life — ḥayawān is an intensive form of 'life': life in its fullest, most vibrant reality; real, lasting life as opposed to a fleeting shadow of it.
12.grammar: The prefix al- is the definite article 'the', marking this as THE life — a specific, known reality. The final -u is the nominative case ending: it marks the word as a subject or as the predicate of an 'is'-statement (what something truly is). Because the word carries 'the', it takes no tanwīn.

13.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
13.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

14.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
14.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
15.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
1.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

2.meaning: They rode / they embarked — to mount or board something that carries you (an animal, a ship); commonly used of boarding a vessel to travel over water.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending means 'they' (a group, at least one male): it tells you the action was completed by a plural subject — 'they rode/boarded'. The silent alif written after the wāw is purely a spelling convention marking the plural ending.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The ship, ark, or vessel — a craft that floats and travels upon water; the word serves as both singular ('ship') and collective ('ships').
4.grammar: A definite noun (the al- prefix means 'the') with the -i (genitive) ending, the case that typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the ship'). The form can denote one ship or ships collectively.
4.root: ف-ل-ك (f-l-k) — ships; also the circling orbit/sphere

5.meaning: They called/invoked — to call upon, summon, or appeal to someone, especially calling on Allah in prayer and supplication. The root spans calling, inviting, and praying.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb. The plural ending (-aw, written with the silent final alif) marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'): 'they called / invoked'.
5.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, pray

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
6.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

7.meaning: Being sincere and single-hearted — making one's devotion purely and exclusively for Allah, with no rival motive mixed in. It describes a group of people in this state.

parts.en: one who is sincere / devotes purely

7.grammar: A Form IV active participle (pattern muf'il, from the verb akhlaṣa 'to make pure / devote sincerely'), describing the one who purifies and dedicates his devotion. It is in the sound masculine plural, and the '-īna' ending marks the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, so it describes a plural group as those who make their worship purely and sincerely for Allah.
7.root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ) — to be pure, sincere, unmixed

8.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
8.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

9.meaning: The dīn — a deep term covering religion, the way of life, the path of obedience and worship owed to Allah, and the reckoning/recompense for it; a complete system of belief and practice with accountability.
9.grammar: A definite noun ('al-' = 'the') with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles.

10.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
10.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

11.meaning: He delivers them / rescues them

parts.en: He delivered / rescued (past tense, Form II)
them (3rd person masculine plural object pronoun)

11.grammar: verb, perfect tense, Form II (نَجَّى), 3rd person masculine singular; with 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun هُمْ
11.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to be saved, to rescue, to deliver

12.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
12.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

13.meaning: The dry land — solid ground as opposed to the sea; the terrain one travels on foot.
13.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or when the word is linked to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship. The doubled r (shadda) is part of the stem.
13.root: ب-ر-ر (b-r-r) — open land; expansiveness

14.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

15.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
15.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

16.meaning: 'They associate (partners with Him)' — an ongoing/present verb. From the root for partnership, this form (causative, Form IV) means to make something a partner or associate, especially to set up partners alongside Allah in worship or divinity (the act underlying shirk).
16.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' doing the action now or habitually. The yu- prefix is the marker of Form IV (causative): 'to make (something) a partner.' The full -ūna ending signals the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not cut short by a governing particle.
16.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; (causative) to associate partners

1.meaning: So that they may deny, reject, or be ungrateful — to cover over a truth or a favour and refuse to acknowledge it.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb after the particle 'li-' ('so that, in order to'), which puts it in the subjunctive of purpose. The 'ya-' prefix marks third-person, and the '-ū' ending marks a masculine-plural subject ('they'); the final 'n' that the plural would otherwise carry drops because of the particle.
1.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, deny, be ungrateful

2.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
2.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

3.meaning: We gave them / We granted them; a completed act of bestowing or providing, done by a "we" subject and directed to a group as recipients.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning "to give/grant." The attached -nā marks the subject as "we" (the doer), and the attached -hum marks "them" as the recipients/object. The form states a completed action.
3.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (in this form) to bring, give, grant

4.meaning: And so that they may enjoy themselves — Form V of m-t-ʿ: to take one's fill of pleasure, to indulge in temporary enjoyment; the li- gives it the sense of purpose or (ominously) 'let them enjoy for a while'.
4.grammar: Wa- is 'and'; li- is a particle of purpose or permission ('so that…', 'let them…'). The ya- prefix plus the -ū ending together mean 'they' (masculine plural) in the present tense. After li-, the verb shifts out of the plain indicative: the usual final nūn (-ūna) is dropped, leaving bare -ū — this shortened ending signals the subjunctive mood of purpose ('that they MAY enjoy') or a command-like 'let them enjoy'.
4.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to enjoy, to benefit temporarily

5.meaning: A two-part marker meaning 'then/so' plus 'shall/will.' It announces something forthcoming as a consequence: the particle sawfa points to the future, generally a more remote or emphatic future than the shorter prefix sa-.
5.grammar: A linking particle fa- ('then/so,' signalling result or sequence) joined to the future particle sawfa, which is placed before a present-tense verb to throw its action into the future ('will/shall …').

6.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
6.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
1.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').

2.meaning: To see, perceive, or behold — and, by extension, to realize, observe, or come to recognize. The bare form here is the 'cut-short' (jussive) shape used after certain particles, so it reads 'they (do not) see'.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in its shortened (jussive) form, used after particles such as those that negate the past or express purpose/condition. The third-person masculine plural subject 'they' here takes the distinct jussive plural ending '-aw' (written wāw + a silent 'alif al-fāriqa). This '-aw' is the jussive paradigm's own ending in its own right, not the indicative '-ūna' with the 'na' stripped off.

3.meaning: That We … — an emphatic linking particle 'that' fused with the pronoun 'We.' 'Anna' introduces and asserts a fact ('that indeed …'), and the attached 'We' names the doer (a majestic or plural 'We').
3.grammar: An emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -nā 'we.' This family of particles takes a following noun/pronoun in the accusative as its subject, so -nā here functions as that subject: 'that We …'. It firmly introduces a stated fact.

4.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
4.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

5.meaning: a sanctuary / a place of safety. Ḥaram refers to a sacred and inviolable place of security — a sanctuary where harm is forbidden and people are protected.

parts.en: a sanctuary, a sacred inviolable place, a place of security (accusative indefinite)

5.grammar: Masculine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), indicated by -an (tanwīn with fatḥa). Object or complement of a preceding verb.
5.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to be forbidden, sacred; ḥaram: the sacred sanctuary

6.meaning: Āmin — safe and secure; a place or person free from fear and danger, enjoying peace and protection.
6.grammar: An indefinite active participle ('safe / secure'). The -an ending is accusative with nunation, commonly marking a descriptive word (modifying an accusative noun) or a predicate; the nunation signals it is indefinite. It describes the quality of being secure and free from fear.
6.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe, secure, free from fear

7.meaning: And (people) are being snatched away — the passive of an intensive verb of seizing: to be abruptly carried off or abducted, taken by force in a swift snatch.
7.grammar: Wa- is 'and/while', attaching this clause to another. The yu- prefix with the internal a-vowels is the passive voice in the present tense: the subject is not doing the snatching but suffering it — 'is/are being snatched'. The final -u is the indicative mood marker, signalling a plain ongoing statement of fact rather than a wish or condition.

8.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
8.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
8.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: Around them — ḥawl means the surrounding space, the area encircling something; with 'them' attached: all about them, on every side of them.
10.grammar: A noun of place used like a preposition ('around'). The -i is the genitive ending: it appears when a word follows a preposition or is linked to what comes after it in an 'of' relationship — here it links ḥawl to its possessor. The suffix -him is 'them' (masculine plural), giving 'the space around them / their surroundings'.
10.root: ح-و-ل (ḥ-w-l) — to surround, turn about; the space around

11.meaning: A cluster of particles plus a noun meaning roughly "Then is it in falsehood …?" — opening a rhetorical question about falsehood or vanity. "Falsehood" here is what is baseless, void, and untrue.
11.grammar: The question marker a- ("is/do?"), connector fa- ("then"), preposition bi- ("in/with"), and the definite article al- attached to a noun. Because of the preposition, "falsehood" takes the genitive -i ending. It frames a rhetorical question.
11.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be void, false, vain, of no effect; falsehood, vanity

12.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
12.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

13.meaning: And in the favor (of) — niʿmah is a blessing or gracious favor: any good freely bestowed, above all the bounties Allah grants; the bi- prefix means 'in/with/by means of'.
13.grammar: Wa- is 'and'; bi- is the preposition 'in/with/by'. Any noun following bi- must take the genitive case, and the -i ending shows exactly that. The genitive here also typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of' relationship — 'the favor OF …' — which is why the form ends in bare -i with no tanwīn.
13.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — grace, favor, ease and bounty

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: 'They disbelieve / reject faith', or more literally 'they cover over (the truth), they are ungrateful'. An ongoing or habitual rejection and denial.
15.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural 'they' acting now or habitually; the final -na (kept, not dropped) shows the verb is in its plain indicative form, stating an ongoing fact.
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — covering over; hence disbelief and ingratitude

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: An elative adjective meaning 'more / most wrongdoing, unjust, or oppressive' — comparing degrees of ẓulm (placing things out of their rightful place, transgression).
2.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) noun on the pattern afʿal, meaning 'more/most unjust'. It ends in -u (nominative), the case typical of a subject or predicate.
2.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, putting something where it does not belong

3.meaning: A combination meaning 'than whoever / than one who' or 'from whoever' — the preposition min ('from/than') merged with man ('who/whoever'). It links a comparison or origin to an unspecified person.
3.grammar: The preposition min ('from', and 'than' in comparisons) fused with the relative/indefinite pronoun man ('who(ever)'). The nūn of min assimilates into the mīm of man, so min + man becomes mimman. The whole final nūn belongs to man, not to min; the kasrah on it (-i) is a liaison (waṣl) vowel added to keep two unvowelled consonants (sukūns) from meeting before the next word. Read together: mimmani, 'than/from the one who'.

4.meaning: 'He fabricated, invented, forged (a lie); he concocted falsely' — made something up and falsely attributed it, especially a lie. A verb of deliberate fabrication.

parts.en: connecting (helping) vowel for the verb pattern
past-tense 3rd person masculine singular ending '-ā' (from a weak final root letter)

4.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he fabricated'). It is a Form VIII (ifta'ala) verb. The final '-ā' (written as alif maqṣūra) is how the past-tense '-a' ending appears when the root ends in a weak letter (w/y). The initial 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the consonant cluster of this pattern be pronounced.
4.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, forge, invent (a falsehood)

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'a lie / falsehood' — a deliberately false statement, an untruth fabricated against the truth.
7.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a lie') with the accusative -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb (e.g. fabricating a lie); the -an tanwīn shows it is indefinite.
7.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to declare false

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
8.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'he denied / cried lies against / rejected as false' — to treat something or someone as a lie, refusing to accept it as true and openly rejecting it.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb (form II, intensive), third-person masculine singular ('he denied / rejected as false'). The doubled middle letter (kadhdhaba) gives the sense of actively declaring something false. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a masculine singular doer.
9.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (form II) to deny, to call a lie

10.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
10.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
10.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the point that' something occurred — pointing to the moment a past event took place and often implying that one thing happened upon the completion of another. In other uses it can carry the sense of 'not yet'.
11.grammar: A particle (a small connecting word), not a noun or verb, so it has no case or tense ending. It introduces a clause and links it in time to another event — most often 'when / as soon as' a past action happened.

12.meaning: It came to him / he came to him — arrival reaching a particular person. The act of coming or arriving, directed toward someone.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it came'), with the final -a marking a completed action; the attached -hu is the object 'him' (the one reached or come to).

13.meaning: "Is it not …? / Is … not …?" A questioning "is not," combining the question-marker "a-" with the negative verb "laysa" ("is not"), used to ask a question that expects the answer "yes, it is."
13.grammar: The negating verb laysa ("is/are not") prefixed with the question-marker a- ("…?"). Such "is it not …?" questions typically invite agreement ("yes, indeed it is"). Laysa is a special verb that negates a statement of being; it carries no tense-ending of the ordinary kind here.

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
15.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
15.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

16.meaning: An abode / a dwelling place — mathwan is a noun meaning a dwelling, a resting place, or an abode — here referring to Hell as the dwelling of the liars.

parts.en: a dwelling, an abode, a resting place

16.grammar: Mathwā is a Form I noun of place (mafʿal pattern) from root th-w-y, meaning a place of staying or dwelling. In the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an). The verse: 'Is there not in Hell an abode (mathwan) for the arrogant?' — rhetorically affirming the punishment awaiting them.
16.root: ث-و-ي (th-w-y) — to stay, to dwell, to reside; a dwelling place

17.meaning: For/to those who reject faith — the active participle 'kāfir' (one who covers over, conceals, and so denies the truth) in its sound masculine plural, preceded by the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to' or 'for'.
17.grammar: The 'li-' prefix means 'to/for'. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, used after a preposition; it marks 'the rejecters' as the object of 'for'. The base is an active participle: 'one who is rejecting/covering up faith'.
17.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and thus reject or disbelieve

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: They strove and struggled with effort — they exerted themselves and fought hard for a cause, expending strength against difficulty or an opponent.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of the III ('mufāʿala') pattern, which conveys effortful, sustained, or mutual action ('to strive/struggle against'). The ending -ū marks a third person masculine plural subject ('they all strove'). The silent alif written after the wāw is a spelling convention for this ending.
2.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — to exert effort, strive, struggle; cf. 'jihād'

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'among us / in us / in our midst,' combining the preposition 'in/among' with the pronoun 'us.'
3.grammar: The preposition fī ('in, among, within') with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('us'). Pronouns attached to prepositions are in the object form; the preposition itself does not change shape.

4.meaning: We will most surely guide them — a solemnly emphasized promise of guidance: to show the way, direct someone onto the right path; the doubled ending stacks oath-like certainty onto the verb.
4.grammar: The la- prefix is the emphatic lām of oath: 'surely, by (Our) oath'. The na- prefix means 'we' — the subject is 'We'. The -anna suffix is the 'energetic' ending, a special form that intensifies a promise or threat: combined with la- it yields 'We will most definitely…'. Finally, -hum is the object pronoun 'them' — the ones who will be guided.
4.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, show the way

5.meaning: 'Our ways / paths / roads' — courses or routes one travels, here possessed by 'us'; figuratively, the manner or course of conduct.
5.grammar: A plural noun, 'ways/paths', with '-nā' = 'our' attached. The '-a' ending marks the accusative case, which commonly identifies the object of a verb or otherwise signals a noun that is acted upon or specified.

6.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
6.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
7.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

8.meaning: Surely (is) with — the preposition maʿa, 'with, in the company of, alongside', fronted by the emphatic la- that stresses the certainty of the accompaniment: 'truly with'.
8.grammar: La- is the emphatic lām, which underlines the truth of the statement it introduces ('is indeed…'). Maʿa is a preposition meaning 'with'; its final -a is its own fixed vowel, not a changing case ending, and whatever noun follows it will stand in the genitive ('with …'). Together: 'is surely with'.

9.meaning: 'The doers of good / those who act with excellence and beauty'. It denotes people who do what is good and do it well — acting righteously, generously, and with sincerity, as if conscious of being watched by Allah.

parts.en: good-doers / those who excel in doing good

9.grammar: A definite plural active participle (the 'doer' form of the verb 'to do good'). The prefixed al- means 'the'. The ending -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the object/oblique state — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. It refers to male (or mixed) persons characterized by the action.
9.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful; to do well and excellently
